headline: Low prompt-injection and cascading-error risk; no shared workspace or sensitive-data pathway is documented between PaddleOCR and RisingWave.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: PaddleOCR ingests documents/images and can run browsers, so hostile content could be parsed as instructions if manually bridged into RisingWave. RisingWave has no documented input channel from PaddleOCR, so the pathway is not default. The interaction is inferred from documented capabilities, not observed integration.
conditions: IF an operator copies PaddleOCR output into RisingWave-controlled prompts or parsers, injection becomes plausible.
IF a shared filesystem or message queue is added between the agents, the risk increases.
mitigations: Keep a human review step between OCR output and any downstream parsing.
Disable browser execution unless needed for a specific job.
Use strict output schemas for PaddleOCR-to-RisingWave handoff.
Store intermediate files in separate directories with read-only access.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging for all transferred text.

B_data_leakage.rationale: PaddleOCR touches documents and images, but RisingWave shows no data classes touched and no shared workspace, OAuth, or upload surface is documented. Without a shared channel, there is no plausible default leakage path from one agent to the other.
conditions: IF both agents are later deployed on the same shared workspace, leakage risk may emerge.
IF RisingWave is configured to ingest PaddleOCR artifacts containing sensitive documents, data exposure becomes possible.
mitigations: Keep the agents on separate workspaces.
Avoid placing sensitive OCR artifacts in shared folders.
Review any future OAuth scopes before enabling them.
Use least-privilege file permissions for intermediate outputs.
requires-engineering: implement per-agent storage isolation.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: PaddleOCR has allowlisted network egress and browser execution, while RisingWave has no documented egress and no write surfaces. There is no evidence of overlapping mutable resources such as shared filesystem writes or git state, so conflict is limited and non-default.
conditions: IF both agents are granted write access to the same directory, write conflicts become plausible.
IF RisingWave is extended with mutable external-resource access, coordination risk increases.
mitigations: Assign separate output directories.
Avoid concurrent writes to shared artifacts.
Run one agent at a time for the same dataset.
Use file locks if a shared directory is unavoidable.
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-level locking for shared resources.

D_cascading_error.rationale: PaddleOCR can produce extracted text from documents/images, and RisingWave is a data-engineering system that could consume such outputs. However, no default action-taking authority or direct handoff is documented, so cascading error requires an explicit pipeline and remains limited by the lack of evidence.
conditions: IF RisingWave is configured to treat PaddleOCR output as authoritative input, downstream errors can cascade.
IF OCR output is auto-ingested without validation, incorrect extractions may propagate.
mitigations: Add validation checks before ingestion.
Require sampling-based human review of OCR output.
Reject low-confidence OCR fields automatically.
Log source-to-destination mappings for traceability.
requires-engineering: add schema validation and confidence thresholds.

E_compliance.rationale: No residency, certification, retention, or subject-rights mismatch is documented for either agent. PaddleOCR touches documents/images, but RisingWave has no declared data classes or compliance constraints here, so a compliance breach pathway is not evidenced.
conditions: IF future deployment routes regulated data through a noncompliant environment, compliance risk may arise.
IF either agent is assigned a regulated data class with stricter residency or retention rules, reassess.
mitigations: Document the data classes each agent may process.
Confirm retention settings before deployment.
Avoid routing regulated data through undocumented pipelines.
Review vendor compliance claims before production use.
requires-engineering: add policy enforcement for residency and retention.
